source.title: Scaling Properties of Diffusion Models for Perceptual Tasks
source.authors: Rahul Ravishankar; Zeeshan Patel; Jathushan Rajasegaran; Jitendra Malik

record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling investigations to image diffusion models used for visual perception, reporting scaling results for pretraining, fine-tuning, and inference.
record.gate_note: The study reports scaling outcomes for diffusion models on visual tasks, so those results bear on V5 and V6. Benchmark comparisons in Tables 3–5 are not scaling sweeps and are not recorded as rows. The study does not test held-out language-model cross-entropy or fixed-compute parameter/token allocation.
record.test_reason: The study reports power-law fits of pretraining loss and fine-tuned depth-estimation metrics against compute for image diffusion transformers (14.8M–1.9B parameters). These are a new modality and a fine-tuning regime for V5, and downstream metrics versus model and pretraining scale for V6. It does not study language-model loss, extrapolation to larger runs, compute-optimal parameter/token splits, shape at fixed size, or fit sensitivity.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that power laws appear across training scaling (model size, pretraining compute, resolution, upcycling) and inference scaling (steps, ensembling, noise schedule) for diffusion-based perception. They also claim performance competitive with the state of the art using far less data and compute.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses image diffusion transformers and visual-perception training or inference metrics, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy and parameter/token/compute sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with model size, pretraining steps, image resolution, expert counts, DDIM sampling steps, ensemble forward-pass count, and noise-variance schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Depth error falls along reported power laws as DDIM sampling steps (1–100) and ensemble size (1–20) increase. The cosine noise schedule beats linear schedules at fixed compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-time (inference) compute scaling in diffusion models improves downstream perception metrics as a power law.

record.problems: The study reports curves mainly through figures, without uncertainty estimates or most numerical curve values. Its generative pretraining result is training loss rather than held-out loss. The scaling studies focus on visual tasks and do not establish the language-model claims.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 3–5 are benchmark comparisons across methods, not scaling outcomes, so they were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fit is used to predict runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute sweep of parameter/token allocation. The 'compute-optimal recipes' are configuration choices, not a fitted optimal-allocation law.
Depth and width are scaled together; no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Only image diffusion on ImageNet-1K and depth fine-tuning on Hypersim. Held-out loss, video, repeated data, and the MoE pretraining scaling (Section 3.2, no curve reported) are not tested.
Only depth estimation. There are no scaling sweeps for optical flow or amodal segmentation, and no prediction of downstream metrics from pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices, schedules or parameter counting; no test of curve bending.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 label wrongly included test-time compute and noise-schedule rows (r11–r16), and the resolution rows (r7, r8) rest on two points each. All scaling evidence is figure-only apart from one fitted pretraining law. There are no uncertainties or fit diagnostics. Tables 3–5 are method comparisons and are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
The fixed-compute optimal parameter/token split and its growth with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
The study tests image diffusion and visual-perception settings, not other non-image modalities, repeated-data regimes, or fine-tuning and transfer outside these visual tasks.
The study tests downstream visual-perception metrics, not language-model downstream tasks or general downstream-task predictability.
Whether exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with setup or fitting choices, or whether curves depart from single power laws.

relationships.condition: Class-conditional DiT pretraining on ImageNet-1K (14.8M–1.9B parameters, fixed 400k iterations) and depth fine-tuning on Hypersim
relationships.reason: Training loss fits L(C)=0.23·C^-0.0098 (r1). Fine-tuning loss and depth metrics follow reported power laws in compute (r2–r6). These are training-loss, figure-only fits with no fit quality reported.
relationships.display_finding: Pretraining loss fitted L(C)=0.23·C^−0.0098, and fine-tuning loss and depth metrics followed reported compute power laws, without reported fit quality.

relationships.condition: Depth estimation on Hypersim after fine-tuning dense DiTs a1–a6, a4 with varied pretraining steps, and upcycled a2–a4
relationships.reason: Depth AbsRel and Delta1 error fall along reported power laws with model size (r3, r4) and pretraining compute (r5, r6). Upcycling improves them by 5.3% and 8.6% on average (r9, r10).
relationships.display_finding: AbsRel and Delta1 errors decrease along power laws with model size and pretraining compute, and upcycling improves them by averages of 5.3% and 8.6%, respectively.
